_note: 'id' is required in practice: it is the account's stable identity key. It keys the
the /api/quota payload, the Homepage widget map (items['<id>_<window>']) and the
error list — so it MUST be unique per account and MUST NOT change once the panel is
running (changing it renames the Homepage widgets). Lowercase letters, digits and
dashes only.
If 'id' is omitted it falls back to a positional '<provider>-<index>', so inserting
or reordering accounts silently reassigns ids between two accounts.
Duplicate ids are fatal: the app refuses to start with
'account ids must be unique: [...]'. 'label' is free text and purely cosmetic.
Credentials: exactly one of 'token' (the key itself), 'token_env' (the NAME of an
environment variable holding it) or 'token_file' (path to a file holding it).
_background_note: Page artwork, as an http(s) URL. The panel downloads it once at container startup and
serves it from /background out of the container's non-persistent /tmp (a tmpfs in the
compose files). The panel bundles no image of its own: a fetch that fails, or an image in
a type it cannot serve, leaves /background answering 404, and the page keeps the colour it
draws itself. The artwork is never a reason for the panel to fail.
Absent or empty means the wallpaper the panel points at by default; its URL is in the README
under background_url, and in app.py as BACKGROUND_URL_DEFAULT. 'none' or 'off' means no
artwork at all, with no fetch, which is what the test suites and an offline install want.

_note: Usage history: /history charts every account window over time. 'path' (also QUOTA_DB)
must be a writable directory the container user owns — a mount at /data, never a single
file, since sqlite writes its journal beside the database. A CIFS/NFS path is refused.
'sample_seconds' is how often a reading is stored; polling is unchanged, only the row
write is gated (measured: ~0.35 GB a year at 300 s, ~1.7 GB at 60 s, plus ~116 MB of
rollups). 'raw_days' of raw samples are kept; older history survives as 'rollup_seconds'
buckets kept 'rollup_days'. A rollup is the long-term record, not a cache of it: a raw
row is dropped only once its bucket exists. 'enabled': false turns the whole layer off —
no database, no volume, no /api/history.

accounts._note: Money-balance providers have no cap, so the card shows the amount instead of a percent.
